intro: Both grant X and then deny what X would lead you to expect. といえども looks at who or what X is (a child, a professional, a single yen): even X is no exception. とはいえ looks at a fact (it is spring, I passed): that is true, but it does not settle the matter. First question: is X a status or category, or a fact you are conceding?

skills.rule: X といえども Y: even X, which you might expect to be an exception, is no exception to Y.
skills.explain:
といえども follows a noun, and less often a plain form. X is a status or category that seems to deserve special treatment: 子ども, 社長, プロ, 一円, 親. Y overturns that expectation, very often as a rule or obligation: ～なければならない, ～てはいけない, ～は許されない, or a realistic ～こともある.

It is formal and written, at home in speeches, rules and editorials. It is often strengthened with たとえ or いかなる: たとえ親といえども, 子どもの手紙を勝手に読んではいけない.

When X is just a fact, とはいえ also works and sounds more natural in conversation: 春といえども寒い and 春とはいえ寒い are both correct. But only とはいえ can stand at the start of a sentence as a conjunction.
patterns: [status / category] といえども、[must / must not / is not allowed]
たとえ [noun] といえども、[rule]
[small amount] といえども、[must not waste]

examples.jp: 子[こ]ども{といえども}、ルールは守[まも]らなければならない。
examples.en: Even children have to keep the rules.

examples.jp: プロの選手[せんしゅ]{といえども}、ミスをすることはある。
examples.en: Even professional players make mistakes sometimes.

examples.jp: 一円[いちえん]{といえども}、無駄[むだ]にしてはいけない。
examples.en: You mustn't waste money, not even a single yen.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]{といえども}、会社[かいしゃ]のお金[かね]を勝手[かって]に使[つか]うことは許[ゆる]されない。
examples.en: Even the president is not allowed to use company money as he likes.

examples.jp: たとえ親[おや]{といえども}、子[こ]どもの手紙[てがみ]を勝手[かって]に読[よ]んではいけない。
examples.en: Not even a parent should read their child's letters without permission.

contrast.note: とはいえ concedes a fact and can open a sentence: とはいえ、～. といえども stresses that even a special status is no exception, and cannot open a sentence.
とあって gives a reason with the expected result: 連休とあって混んでいた. といえども says the result goes against expectation.
ながらも joins two states of the same subject: 狭いながらも快適な部屋. It follows verbs and adjectives, not a status noun.

mistakes.bad: 連休[れんきゅう]{といえども}、道[みち]がひどく混[こ]んでいた。
mistakes.good: 連休[れんきゅう]とあって、道[みち]がひどく混[こ]んでいた。
mistakes.note: Crowds are what a long weekend leads you to expect, so this is a reason: とあって.

mistakes.bad: 先生[せんせい]{といえども}、何[なん]でもよく知[し]っている。
mistakes.good: 先生[せんせい]{といえども}、知[し]らないことはある。
mistakes.note: Y must go against what X suggests; a teacher knowing a lot is no surprise.

skills.tip: Insert "even" before X and expect a "still" after it: "even a child must still ...". If that fits and X is a status, it is といえども.

skills.rule: X とはいえ Y: X is true, granted, but it does not lead to what you would expect.
skills.explain:
とはいえ follows a noun or な-adjective (with or without だ), or the plain form of a verb or い-adjective: 春とはいえ, 便利だとはいえ, 合格したとはいえ, 安いとはいえ. It concedes a fact the listener already accepts and then limits it: it is spring, but still cold; it is cheap, but eating out every day is too much.

It also works as a conjunction at the start of a sentence, "that said": この仕事は大変だ。とはいえ、やりがいもある. ものの and ながらも cannot do this.

The second half is free: a fact, a judgment, advice (油断しないほうがいい) or an intention. That makes it more flexible than ものの. It is neutral to formal and common in both speech and writing.
patterns: [verb past] とはいえ、[advice: ～ほうがいい]

examples.jp: 春[はる]{とはいえ}、まだ寒[さむ]い日[ひ]が続[つづ]いている。
examples.en: It may be spring, but the cold days are continuing.

examples.jp: 安[やす]い{とはいえ}、毎日[まいにち]外食[がいしょく]するのは無理[むり]だ。
examples.en: It's cheap, granted, but eating out every day is out of the question.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]に十年[じゅうねん]住[す]んでいる{とはいえ}、敬語[けいご]はまだ難[むずか]しい。
examples.en: I've lived in Japan for ten years, but honorifics are still hard for me.

examples.jp: 試験[しけん]に合格[ごうかく]した{とはいえ}、油断[ゆだん]しないほうがいい。
examples.en: You've passed the exam, true, but you shouldn't get complacent.

examples.jp: この仕事[しごと]は大変[たいへん]だ。{とはいえ}、やりがいもある。
examples.en: This job is hard. That said, it's also rewarding.

contrast.note: といえども is stiffer and centres on a status: 子どもといえども. とはいえ centres on a conceded fact and can begin a sentence.
ものの also concedes a fact (買ったものの使っていない), but it cannot open a sentence and its second half is rarely advice or a plan.
ながらも links two states of one subject and attaches to verb stems or adjectives: 知りながらも. とはいえ concedes a whole fact.

mistakes.bad: 料理[りょうり]は得意[とくい]ではない。{ものの}、毎日[まいにち]作[つく]っている。
mistakes.good: 料理[りょうり]は得意[とくい]ではない。{とはいえ}、毎日[まいにち]作[つく]っている。
mistakes.note: Only とはいえ can start a sentence as "that said".

mistakes.bad: 雨[あめ]{とはいえ}、試合[しあい]は中止[ちゅうし]になった。
mistakes.good: 雨[あめ]のため、試合[しあい]は中止[ちゅうし]になった。
mistakes.note: Rain causing a cancellation is a reason, not a concession; とはいえ needs a result that goes against X.

skills.tip: Say "granted, X, but ..." or "that said, ...". If it fits, it is とはいえ.
